On May 23, 2003, one order signed by the U.S.-led occupation authority dissolved Iraq's entire army.

Somewhere between 230,000 and half a million men lost their jobs. Nobody agrees on the exact number.

President Bush later said: "The policy was to keep the army intact; didn't happen." The man who signed it said Bush was told in advance.

In December 2004, a detainee named Ibrahim al-Badry walked out of an American camp called Camp Bucca.

In June 2014, under the name Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, he was named caliph of a self-declared "Islamic State."

Did one order create ISIS? No. But it's very hard to tell the story of ISIS without it.

The full file is on the channel. The American File.
